chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them).

Regarding the man who escorts his brother for a journey of a day, or two days, or three. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is during the month of Ramadan, let him break his fast.' I said, 'Which is superior: fasting or escorting him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Escorting him. Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has exempted it from him.'

key_terms.وَضَعَهُ: He has exempted it / removed the obligation
key_terms.يُشَيِّعُ: to escort or accompany a traveler

ai.seo_question: Is it better to fast or escort a traveler during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the high status of social duties (birr al-akh) by prioritizing the physical act of escorting a traveler over the ritual of fasting in Ramadan. The Imam’s ruling that the fast is 'removed' (wadh') implies a complete exemption rather than mere postponement, underscoring the weight of companionship in Shia jurisprudence. This reflects the principle that maintaining kinship and social bonds can supersede individual acts of worship when they involve significant effort or distance.
